label: models/fw_walllamp.mdl: a caged wall lamp with a sodium-orange glass

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_357.mdl, models/w_rpgammo.mdl, models/w_chainammo.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked B, D, D, C where the asset was A, B, D, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline reads as a caged wall lamp: a tall flat backplate (right in the side views), a box housing projecting from it, and a bar cage round the glass on the front, sides and underside. Every view has the same parts in the same places, with nothing sticking out or missing.

M2.reason: The brief gives no size for the wall lamp, so there is nothing to be off from. The measured 14 x 16 x 26 units reads as a plausible wall lamp beside Valve's props in the line-up, so nothing here is wrong.

M3.reason: The brief asks for a caged lamp with sodium-orange glass. Those are there: the cage bars cover the front (about six vertical and seven horizontal), the sides, the top and the underside (front-left, back-left and below views); the orange glass panel sits inside; the housing box is behind the cage; and the backplate and top hood are present (top view). No small part the brief names is missing, and no round part is in the brief.

M4.reason: Each region reads as its material: the backplate and housing are painted grey-green metal, the cage is black steel, and the glass is a lit sodium orange (front and front-left views). Nothing is in a colour the brief does not ask for.

M5.reason: The brief asks for no markings. The backplate has faint grime mottling and the edges are bevelled and worn, which suits the palette. The lit glass shows through the cage grid cleanly. Nothing is added that is wrong.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rule that M6 is measured apart. In the line-up test the asset was caught twice of four: at D when the judge picked D (third reading) and at C when the judge picked C (fourth reading). Under three catches, so it passes. Beside the other Valve props it reads as a wall lamp of the same style.

M7.reason: The brief sets no facing. The model stands upright, the backplate is behind, the housing and cage project forward, and the glass faces out from the wall (front and right views). Its origin cannot be checked here, but the mount reads as a wall fitting.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors. At 48 triangles it is well under the median of 99 for Valve's props of its kind. The housing, cage and plate join in the side and back-left views, and the parts a player can see (the underside flange, the top hood) are closed, with nothing floating.
